Sezgen, O., Franconi, E.M., Koomey, J.G., Greenberg, S.E., Afzal, A. and Shown, L. (1995). Technology Data Characterizing Space Conditioning in Commercial Buildings: Application to End-Use Forecasting with COMMEND 4.0. Report LBL-37065 (UC-1600), Ernest Orlando Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, Berkeley, CA, December 1995. No DOI printed.

175-page report on commercial-building HVAC for the COMMEND model; locators are printed page numbers (front matter in roman numerals; PDF page not equal to printed). Commercial buildings are out of scope; only plant equipment that overlaps heat supply was loaded: heating plant boilers (Table 6.10: electric boiler, typical gas boiler, oil boiler; Means 1992 and EPRI 1988 cost columns), cooling plant chillers (Table 6.12), combined air-source and water-loop heat pumps (Table 6.11) and the seasonal efficiency/COP table (6.13) for boilers, heat pumps and chillers. Furnaces, window units, electric packaged and gas packaged units, shell measures, distribution systems, economizers, prototype simulations and service demand were not loaded. Traps: (1) costs are 1992 dollars (Means) or 1986 dollars (EPRI 1988, printed as 1986$); (2) a cost point is size specific, one process per capacity point; (3) Table 6.11 heating capacity quoted is auxiliary resistance heat only, and heat pump costs are per ton of cooling; (4) the gas chiller cost is per square foot of floor area; (5) seasonal efficiencies (stock average vs new-construction marginal) include degradation and part-load losses (stock gas boiler 0.60); (6) the efficient gas boiler cost is only given as about 30% above a regular boiler (other-values); (7) table page numbers inferred (Tables 6.11 and 6.12 share printed pages 50-51 without a visible page marker).
